notes: Source of truth for docs/PLATFORMS.md's generated capability matrix (E20-S03, hardened after round-1 independent verifier review). Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/check_platforms.py generate`. `scripts/check_platforms.py check` cross-validates every claim here: CI presence against .github/workflows/rust.yml's real matrix, each capability's evidence against real #[test] functions found at the exact cited file, and (offline-checkable) that verified_commit is a real ancestor of HEAD - a platform cannot be declared tier 1, or a capability 'verified', by editing prose alone.

platforms.title: macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel)
platforms.notes: Full CI (check + quality: fmt/clippy/test/cargo-deny) on macos-latest, confirmed via a real successful GitHub Actions run for verified_commit. Real identity (device/inode, E03-S01) and real, adversarially-tested deletion (E03-S05/E21-S07) are both verified on this platform's own CI - predates and is unaffected by E20's Windows/WSL work.

platforms.title: Linux (x86_64, glibc)
platforms.notes: Same Unix code path and same tests as macOS, run on its own ubuntu-latest CI - not assumed identical from macOS's result alone. E07-S05 found and fixed a real Linux-specific timing divergence (inode reuse on same-second delete-recreate) that macOS CI alone had never surfaced, which is why this platform is verified independently rather than inferred from macOS.

platforms.title: Windows native (x86_64)
platforms.notes: E20-S01/ADR-0020 implemented real Windows file/volume identity and added real adversarial fixtures (a genuine NTFS junction via mklink /J, a real directory symlink, real hard-links, and a synthetic cross-volume boundary test) - listed here as evidence that the *code and tests exist and are believed correct*, not yet as 'verified': E20-S01 round-1 independent verifier review found this exact commit range had never actually run on GitHub's real windows-latest/ubuntu-latest CI (the branch had not been pushed). `identity.state` stays 'unverified' until a `verified_commit` here has a real, `gh`-confirmed successful rust.yml run. Real deletion remains unimplemented on Windows (`confirmed_delete_file`'s cfg(not(unix)) arm and `cancellai-sealedfs::SealedRoot`'s no-follow walk both refuse unconditionally), so `clean` is inspect-only there regardless of identity verification status.

platforms.title: WSL2 (Windows host, Linux guest)
platforms.notes: No dedicated CI runner exists for WSL2 in this repository (GitHub Actions has no WSL2 runner image). E20-S03 round-1 independent verifier review found this repository's own claim ('non-tier-1 platforms remain inspect-only or refused') was not actually true for WSL2: the generic Unix mutation path took no notice of it at all. Repaired: `cancellai-platform::mutation::confirmed_delete_file` now calls `refuse_unverified_wsl2_mutation` and refuses unconditionally on a detected WSL2 guest until this platform earns its own verified_commit - mutation.state is 'unsupported' by enforced code, not merely by unverified inference from Linux's tier. identity.state stays 'unverified' for the same reason as before: a WSL2 guest is a real Linux kernel, so the Unix identity path would very likely work, but that is an inference this repository has not verified directly.
